content.user_title: Build Modern Interfaces with Tailwind CSS v4
content.value_statement: Tailwind CSS v4 changes configuration and responsive design patterns. This skill provides focused guidance for themes, layouts, tokens, dark mode, and components.
actual_capabilities: Explains CSS-first theme configuration with semantic design tokens.
Selects viewport breakpoints or container queries for responsive layouts.
Suggests Flexbox and CSS Grid utility patterns for common layouts.
Defines light and dark theme utility combinations.
Organizes typography, color, spacing, animation, and transition choices.
Recommends when to extract repeated utility combinations into components.
limitations: Covers Tailwind CSS v4 and does not provide complete v3 migration instructions.
Provides guidance only and does not run builds or inspect rendered pages.
Does not replace project-specific accessibility, browser, or performance testing.
Includes representative patterns rather than a complete Tailwind utility reference.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Basic Utilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest Tailwind CSS v4 utilities for this interface: [describe interface]. Include mobile-first spacing, typography, and layout choices.

prompt_templates.title: Define a CSS-First Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tailwind CSS v4 theme for [product]. Define semantic color, spacing, and font tokens, then explain each naming choice.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Component Responsive
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component structure: [describe structure]. Choose viewport breakpoints or container queries, and specify responsive layout behavior for each size.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Tailwind Design System
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Tailwind CSS v4 conventions: [describe conventions]. Identify arbitrary values, repeated classes, token gaps, dark-mode issues, and extraction opportunities.

output_examples.input: Plan a responsive product card that can appear in narrow and wide parent containers.
output: Use the parent as a named container.
Stack image and content at narrow container widths.
Switch to a two-column layout when the card container has sufficient width.
Keep spacing and typography tied to the shared design-token scale.

output_examples.input: Recommend a maintainable dark-mode strategy for a dashboard with manual theme control.
output_examples.output: Use a class-based theme selector and semantic surface, text, and border tokens. Apply dark variants consistently and test contrast in both themes.

best_practices: Start with mobile styles, then add larger responsive variants only where the layout requires them.
Use semantic CSS variables for shared color, spacing, and typography decisions.
Extract repeated or state-heavy class combinations into framework components.
anti_patterns: Do not scatter arbitrary values when the design system can define a reusable token.
Do not construct utility classes dynamically because the compiler may not detect them.
Do not mix legacy Tailwind v3 configuration patterns into a CSS-first v4 setup.

faq.question: Does this skill support Tailwind CSS v3?
faq.answer: It focuses on Tailwind CSS v4. Some utility concepts apply to v3, but configuration guidance assumes CSS-first v4 patterns.

faq.question: Can it create a complete Tailwind theme?
faq.answer: It can propose semantic color, spacing, and typography tokens. You should validate values against brand and accessibility requirements.

faq.question: When should I use container queries?
faq.answer: Use them when a reusable component must respond to parent width. Use viewport breakpoints for page-level layout changes.

faq.question: Does it generate framework components?
faq.answer: It can recommend component boundaries and utility combinations. Framework-specific implementation still depends on your project structure and conventions.

faq.question: Can it validate accessibility?
faq.answer: It can suggest accessible patterns, but it does not perform contrast calculations, keyboard testing, or assistive technology testing.

faq.question: Does it execute Tailwind or build commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides written guidance and examples without running commands, accessing files, or contacting external services.
